papers.title: Data-driven Distributionally Robust Optimization Using the Wasserstein Metric: Performance Guarantees and Tractable Reformulations
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic programs where the distribution of the uncertain parameters is only observable through a finite training dataset. Using the Wasserstein metric, we construct a ball in the space of (multivariate and non-discrete) probability distributions centered at the uniform distribution on the training samples, and we seek decisions that perform best in view of the worst-case distribution within this Wasserstein ball. The state-of-the-art methods for solving the resulting distributionally robust optimization problems rely on global optimization techniques, which quickly become computationally excruciating. In this paper we demonstrate that, under mild assumptions, the distributionally robust optimization problems over Wasserstein balls can in fact be reformulated as finite convex programs---in many interesting cases even as tractable linear programs. Leveraging recent measure concentration results, we also show that their solutions enjoy powerful finite-sample performance guarantees. Our theoretical results are exemplified in mean-risk portfolio optimization as well as uncertainty quantification.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注数据驱动的分布鲁棒优化，与代理模型和有限元分析的直接关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate model construction, simulation cost reduction, or any specific application to finite element analysis or biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过Wasserstein度量构建数据驱动的分布鲁棒优化，解决样本外性能问题。
summary_zh.method: 将分布鲁棒优化问题重新表述为有限凸规划，甚至线性规划。
summary_zh.result: 在温和假设下得到可求解的形式，并给出有限样本性能保证。
summary_zh.validation: 在均值-风险投资组合优化和不确定性量化中验证。

summary_en.motivation: To solve distributionally robust optimization problems using Wasserstein balls around empirical distributions, providing tractable reformulations and finite-sample guarantees.
summary_en.method: Under mild assumptions, reformulates the optimization over Wasserstein balls as finite convex programs, often linear programs.
summary_en.result: Demonstrates that solutions enjoy powerful finite-sample performance guarantees, with examples in portfolio optimization and uncertainty quantification.
summary_en.validation: Validated on mean-risk portfolio optimization and uncertainty quantification examples.

papers.title: Prospective, Randomized Trial to Evaluate Efficacy of a Bipolar Sealer in Direct Anterior Approach Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.first_author_affiliation: Cleveland Clinic Florida, Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Weston, Florida

corresponding_authors.name: Eric M. Slotkin
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Orthopaedic Associates of Reading, Reading Hospital, West Reading, Pennsylvania

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅涉及全髋关节置换术的临床疗效评估，未涉及生物力学建模或植入物应力分析。
llm.why_not_core: No quantification of femoral stress/strain or micromotion; no FEA or contact modeling; purely clinical outcomes.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估双极凝血器在直接前路全髋置换术中的临床效果。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性随机对照试验，比较双极凝血器与标准电凝的出血量和输血率。
summary_zh.result: 双极凝血器组出血量和输血率显著降低。
summary_zh.validation: 通过随机对照试验进行临床验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of a bipolar sealer in reducing blood loss and transfusion rates during direct anterior approach total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Prospective randomized controlled trial comparing bipolar sealer with standard electrocautery.
summary_en.result: Significant reduction in blood loss and transfusion requirements in the bipolar sealer group.
summary_en.validation: Clinical validation via randomized controlled trial.
